purpose: Control how the archive names places, causes, trajectories, institutions, and contested or stigmatized deaths.

rules.rule: Name the setting only when it helps orientation, dignity, review, or accountability; do not use setting as stigma.
Use person-first or family-preferred language where relevant; never reduce a record to place, cause, or institutional category.
For suicide or overdose settings, omit methods, substances, quantities, paraphernalia, and scene mechanics.
examples: name the aftermath setting, not the method

rules.rule: Do not make public-health data speak as bedside testimony.
examples: statistics can justify a coverage gap; they cannot supply what the room felt like

rules.rule: Do not enforce closure language on families without bodies, exact times, or clear narratives.
examples: avoid “at least you know” or “moving on” framings

rules.rule: For children, babies, and pregnancy-related deaths, preserve the family’s chosen relationship words and do not publish intimate material by default.
examples: baby, child, son, daughter, fetus, pregnancy, mother, parent — source-bound and family-led

rules.rule: Never imply that home, hospice, hospital, ICU, or care home automatically means a better or worse death.
examples: describe the affordance; do not assign moral rank

banned_or_restricted_moves: suicide as a puzzle to solve
custody death as only an official-report category
unhoused death as anonymous by default
disaster dead as risk objects rather than persons
pediatric death as sentimental training material
family money conflict as comedy or gossip
public_surface_requirement: Any reader-facing version must include relevant nonclaims before or beside the content, not hidden in a footer.
rev0012_perspective_axis_note: Public rendering must distinguish witness role, account type, authority boundary, and missing perspectives before clinical, setting, or practice interpretation.
